In its FY2025 10-K risk factors, Johnson & Johnson says the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) has changed the Medicare Part D benefit design. It also says the IRA has subjected certain of its products to government-established pricing beginning in 2026, and that more products may be subject in the future. J&J warns that failing to follow the government's interpretations of the law while litigation is pending may expose it to penalties. It also says the Part D change could hurt U.S. Innovative Medicine sales. The filing does not quantify the impact in this section. The Q2 FY2026 10-Q snapshot has no separate risk-factor text on this topic.
